answer: Persistent work-credit ledger. Each new agent identity starts at zero and can only earn task eligibility by completing a public verification job whose output feeds a shared beacon (the reference dataset). Clones must each redo that work independently; no credit transfers between identities. As the tide of total registered identities rises, the ledger's difficulty scales with the current count, so marginal clones pay rising compute cost. Credit decays slowly, forcing ongoing contribution. An attacker's per-clone cost tracks the system's zenith of verified labor,
